meta.note: Pattern-strategy skill library (paper Sec. 4.2). Entries marked source=seed are textbook transformations offered as untested suggestions: they carry zero occurrences and zero confidence and must earn their statistics from real runs, exactly like a learned entry. Entries gain occurrences, SEC-pass counts and a mean relative advantage A_i as the loop runs, and are demoted to status=invalid if they break equivalence more often than not.

skills.pattern: carry propagation across a wide accumulator
skills.strategy: accumulate in carry-save form and resolve with a single carry-propagate adder
skills.rationale: Each full-width add resolves a carry chain. Keeping the running total as a redundant (sum, carry) pair makes every intermediate add a constant-depth 3:2 compression, and only the last step pays for a carry chain.
skills.example:
// keep {s, c} redundant through the chain, resolve once at the end
wire [W:0] total = s + c;

skills.strategy: pre-decode the next state one cycle early and register the decoded form
skills.rationale: Decoding a binary state register into control signals puts a decoder in series with everything it controls. Registering the decoded (one-hot) form moves the decode off the consuming path without adding latency, because the decode of the *next* state is computable this cycle.

skills.pattern: high-fanout signal on the critical path
skills.strategy: replicate the driver so each load group has its own copy
skills.rationale: A net driving many loads needs a big driver or a buffer tree; both cost delay on the launching path. Duplicating the logic that produces it splits the load without changing the value.
skills.example:
reg sel_a, sel_b;  // two copies of one condition
always @(posedge clk) begin sel_a <= cond; sel_b <= cond; end

skills.pattern: long path through an operand shared by many consumers
skills.strategy: isolate the operand per consumer so an idle consumer stops loading it
skills.rationale: Operand isolation removes both switching power and capacitive load from the shared net, shortening the path that drives it.

skills.strategy: flatten the serial mux chain into a single balanced select
skills.rationale: Nested conditionals synthesise to a chain of 2:1 muxes with depth equal to the nesting. A one-hot or case-based select of the same conditions gives one balanced level of selection instead.

skills.strategy: reduce with a balanced tree instead of a linear priority scan
skills.rationale: A linear priority chain has depth proportional to width. A tree reduction that combines (found, index) pairs pairwise has logarithmic depth and the same result.
skills.example: // combine pairwise: (found_hi ? idx_hi : idx_lo) up the tree

skills.pattern: reset logic in series with the datapath
skills.strategy: move the reset out of the data path and onto the register's own reset
skills.rationale: A reset ANDed into the data expression puts a gate in series with the whole datapath. Using the flop's reset port keeps the datapath clean.

skills.pattern: saturation or clamp after a long arithmetic path
skills.strategy: form the clamp condition beside the arithmetic and apply it as a select, not as a compare-then-select
skills.rationale: A clamp written as compare-then-mux serialises three things: the arithmetic, the comparison, and the selection. The condition usually depends on high bits and overflow flags that the arithmetic produces before its low bits settle.

skills.strategy: rebalance the chain into an adder tree
skills.rationale: A left-to-right chain of N adds has depth N-1; a balanced tree has ceil(log2 N). The arithmetic result is identical because integer addition is associative in two's complement of a fixed width.

skills.pattern: sign extension replicated before every operand of a wide add
skills.strategy: add the narrow values and sign-extend once at the end
skills.rationale: Sign-extending each product to the accumulator width before adding makes every adder full-width. Adding at the natural width and extending the single result gives the same value with narrower carry chains.

skills.pattern: unpipelined multiplier array in one cycle
skills.strategy: redistribute the existing registers across the array without changing the latency
skills.rationale: When the module already has registers before and after the multiply, the boundary between them can be moved into the array -- retiming -- so each stage carries less depth. Total latency is unchanged, which is what the equivalence check requires.
skills.example:
// move the input register past the partial-product stage rather than
// adding a new one: latency in == latency out.

skills.pattern: wide comparison at the end of the datapath
skills.strategy: precompute the comparison from partial results in parallel with the final arithmetic
skills.rationale: A compare that waits for the full sum adds its own carry chain on top of the datapath's. The deciding bits are usually available earlier -- the sign and the bits above the limit -- so the condition can be formed beside the sum instead of after it.
